fields.question: How can sparse verifier feedback reach unsampled tokens?
fields.answer: Project response-level verifier preference onto cumulative teacher/reference reward, then hold group statistics fixed and use full-vocabulary log ratios at visited prefixes. This reuses distributions rather than guessing correctness of unsampled responses.
fields.example: Teaching example: when high-D responses usually succeed, c is positive and an unsampled token receives a dense gradient from its teacher/reference ratio. Its possible continuations have not all been verified.

fields.question: Which expectation is preserved by Rao–Blackwellization?
fields.answer: The local gradient expectation after the immediate-token approximation, conditional on the observed group/prefix and a fresh hypothetical next token. Fixed c and baseline permit score-identity cancellation; this is not an unbiased full-sequence verifier gradient.
fields.example: Teaching example: with fixed p=(0.2,0.8), enumerating two next tokens removes that sampling noise, not randomness in the already sampled group or future continuations.

fields.question: Is VOPD lambda GKD's student-data fraction?
fields.answer: No. GKD's mixture changes the source of prefixes. VOPD lambda scales teacher/reference extrapolation with group correlation c. Equal verifier outcomes use fixed0.25 extrapolation, not an invented c=0 fallback.
fields.example: Teaching example: lambda0.25 and c−0.8 give strength−0.2, moving the target toward reference. A GKD data fraction cannot express that operation with a negative value.

fields.question: Why not claim reproduction of top-16 training?
fields.answer: The author repository currently only announces a future release, so trainer reduction details are not source-verified. Local code faithfully executes the theoretical finite full-vocabulary loss/gradient with supplied rewards/distributions, without rollout, models or a verifier.
fields.example: Teaching example: checking all gradients and equivalent targets in a three-token vocabulary does not execute the paper's eight-A1004B training.

fields.question: Why can DPO not express a preference triangle cycle?
fields.answer: Its pair logit is a difference of scalar potentials, so three edges telescope to zero. SHPO adds antisymmetric plane residuals with nonzero triangle circulation rather than enlarging the same BT scalar reward.
fields.example: Teaching example: three scalars cannot satisfy A>B, B>C and C>A. Unit-circle embeddings at0/120/240 degrees can give all three oriented plane areas the same sign.

fields.question: Is the curl head an exact orthogonal Hodge projection?
fields.answer: No. Remark3 explicitly describes a parametric antisymmetric head, not necessarily the fixed graph's orthogonal curl projection. Harmonic-free assumptions also exclude some global topological cycles. Swapping sign is only one structural property.
fields.example: Teaching example: oriented area is antisymmetric, but without solving the graph-level least-squares problem it is not an exact graph decomposition.

fields.question: Can augmented-head preference accuracy replace generation quality?
fields.answer: No. Acc_pi uses policy sequence probabilities, acc_dpo corrects by reference and acc_dpo+c adds the head. Generation does not automatically use this pairwise head. Preserve metric definitions and separate generation evaluation.
fields.example: Teaching example: fitting only the head can improve pair classification with an unchanged policy, without directly changing next-token probabilities.

fields.question: How does the local kernel avoid silently using the detach variant?
fields.answer: It returns analytic W, gamma and both input-hidden gradients, all checked by finite differences. A generic nonzero head must have hidden gradients. Zero-projection backward and gamma=0 subgradient choices are explicit local conventions, not upstream defaults.
fields.example: Teaching example: alpha0 makes curl hidden gradients zero; generic nonzero alpha should not. Tests distinguish them without presenting frozen-input calculations as joint model training.
